finalists.label: Tricuspid Atresia
finalists.why: It has the most specific and decisive findings, including severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice, and severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects.

finalists.label: Congenital Heart Disease
finalists.why: It is supported by several key findings, including severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice, and severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects.

frontier_selector.why: Tricuspid Atresia is chosen because it specifically accounts for the severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects, which are not fully explained by Congenital Heart Disease.
